key_insight: Scaffold sparsifies graphs for GNNs by keeping a support that jointly limits rerouting path length (dilation) and load concentration (congestion), preserving communication structure while cutting edges.
engineering_relevance: It lowers GNN memory and training cost on large graphs, offering a practical way to approximate full-graph performance with far fewer edges.
method: Derives sparsification from support graph theory preconditioners.
Controls two structural criteria: dilation and congestion.
Selects sparse supports that retain short, well-distributed message-passing routes.
evidence_signal: Across 19 homophilic and heterophilic benchmarks, Scaffold achieved the best aggregate rank and often matched full-graph performance using only 10%–50% of edges.
watch_item: Sparsification quality depends on tuning the support so that edge reduction does not create long rerouting paths or bottlenecked congestion, especially on highly irregular graphs.
paper_title: Scaffold: Support Graph Theory Based Sparsification for Graph Neural Networks
